chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Wahb ibn Munabbah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, peace be upon them both,
Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) said: 'Yasammata' is said to the sneezer three times; whatever is above that is due to the air.

key_terms.يُسَمَّتُ: A verbal noun or passive form referring to the saying of the specific phrase (Yarhamuk Allah) to the sneezer

ai.seo_question: How many times should one say 'Yarhamuk Allah' when someone sneezes according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, transmitted via the reliable chain of al-Saduq, establishes a specific jurisprudential boundary for the etiquette of sneezing (Adab al-'Atas). It distinguishes between the first three sneezes, which are considered part of the same event warranting the supplication 'Yarhamuk Allah', and subsequent sneezes, which are attributed to natural airflow (Rih) and thus do not require the same religious response, reflecting the Shia emphasis on precise ritual etiquette.
